pages.title: Request a proposal
pages.content:
Request

We provide fixed-fee proposals for cost planning, bill of quantities, and tender review services within two working days. Contact our Rotterdam studio with your project details to begin.

01

Send drawings

02

Fixed-fee proposal

03

30-minute call

04

Concept cost plan

01

Four-Step Proposal Process

Our engagement process follows four transparent steps. Step 01: You send us your drawings, project brief, and site address. Step 02: We review the documentation and reply with a fixed-fee proposal within two working days. Step 03: We host a focused 30-minute introductory call with the partner who will directly price your building to align on scope and milestones. Step 04: Work begins promptly upon approval. We deliver concept cost plans within 10 working days and detailed cost plans within 20 working days, accompanied by our risk register and direct presentation.

02

What Material to Send Us

To enable our client desk to issue a precise fixed fee, please provide whatever architectural information is currently available. This typically includes existing and proposed floor plans, building sections, external elevations, site boundary layouts, and a brief description of project objectives. For feasibility reviews, early massing diagrams or sketch models are sufficient. For detailed cost plans or bills of quantities, developed design drawings and outline specifications help us establish the exact measurement scope. All project files are treated under strict professional confidentiality.

03

Studio Address and Working Hours

Sekisan Partners is located at Maaskade 41, 3071 NB Rotterdam, Netherlands. Our working hours are Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 17:30 CET. We operate on a phone-free basis, directing all client communications and technical submissions through proposals@sekisan.example. Noor Haddad monitors incoming proposals and ensures prompt routing to the appropriate partner. All consulting fees are quoted in EUR excl. VAT, and our invoices are payable within 30 days from invoice issue. We look forward to evaluating your forthcoming development.

Q

What material is required to receive a fixed-fee proposal?

You do not need fully detailed construction packages to request a fee proposal. For concept cost planning, preliminary sketch layouts, a site address, and approximate target floor areas are entirely sufficient. For tender reviews or second opinions, sending the existing bill of quantities or contractor submission allows us to assess the required analytical hours. Once we receive your files by email, our client desk reviews the scope and returns a formal, fixed-price proposal within two working days, outlining deliverables, partner assignment, and project timelines.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Founded in 2011 in Rotterdam, Sekisan Partners provides independent building cost consultancy for clients who require financial certainty before construction begins. We produce rigorous cost plans that establish clear figures before contractors are invited to tender.

01

Founded 2011

02

People

03

The studio

01

Founded 2011: Independent Cost Planning

Ilse van Damme established Sekisan Partners in 2011 after stepping away from a major commercial contractor's estimating desk. During years of pricing building works from the contractor's perspective, she saw that clients consistently received cost advice too late in the design process to influence critical outcomes. By the time tenders landed, design decisions had solidified, leaving value engineering as an aggressive, reductive compromise. Sekisan Partners was formed to change that sequence entirely. Operating from our studio at Maaskade 41 in Rotterdam, we work exclusively on behalf of building owners, public authorities, and design teams. We price projects from first principles while sketches are still flexible, ensuring that the budget approved at concept stage remains the benchmark through completed handover.

Priced before the first spade, since 2011.

02

People: Leadership and Core Estimators

Our practice relies on seven dedicated professionals working collaboratively across every stage of procurement. Ilse van Damme, founding partner and chartered quantity surveyor, guides project strategy and commercial alignment. Tomás Ferreira, partner, leads concept and feasibility cost plans, translating early architectural sketches into robust financial frameworks. Amara Okonjo, senior estimator, directs quantity measurement and the preparation of comprehensive bills of quantities using international measurement standards. Lukas Brandt manages tender review and contractor comparison, interrogating bid returns line by line. Mei-Lin Chou coordinates cost monitoring on active construction sites. Hana Sato oversees empirical cost data and edits our quarterly publication. Noor Haddad manages our client desk, coordinating initial inquiries and proposals within two working days.

03

The Studio: How We Work with Architects

We believe effective cost consultancy supports architectural ambition rather than curbing it. When appointed alongside the design team at early stages, we build dynamic elemental cost models that reflect structural, environmental, and material intentions. We attend design workshops, test multiple construction typologies, and measure quantities directly from preliminary models. Rather than delivering blunt negative feedback, we illuminate where capital is concentrated across the building assembly. This collaborative discipline gives architects the freedom to detail high-value focal spaces while maintaining strict commercial control across repetitive packages. By establishing clarity on structural frames, facade envelopes, and building services early, we prevent the costly disruptions of late-stage redesign.

Q

Where is our studio located and what are our working hours?

Sekisan Partners operates from a dedicated studio located at Maaskade 41, 3071 NB Rotterdam, Netherlands. Our practice is open Monday through Friday from 08:30 to 17:30 CET. We maintain an independent, phone-free workflow to ensure uninterrupted concentration when measuring drawings and analyzing tender returns. Clients and design teams correspond with us directly via proposals@sekisan.example. Inquiries regarding new commissions, peer reviews, or feasibility studies are reviewed daily by our client desk. Following receipt of preliminary project drawings and site details, we issue comprehensive, fixed-fee proposals within two working days, followed by a direct technical consultation.

Request a proposal

pages.title: How we estimate
pages.content:
Method

Our estimating methodology translates architectural drawings into dependable financial figures through five sequential stages. Every cost plan is built from first principles using current market data and international measurement standards.

01

Read the drawings

02

Measure the quantities

03

Price at current rates

04

Write down the risks

05

Hand over and explain

01

Read the Drawings

Every estimate begins with an exhaustive forensic examination of the architectural and engineering information. We do not skim drawings or rely on coarse area multipliers. Our team reviews plans, building sections, structural layouts, and outline specifications to understand construction sequencing, structural grids, foundation requirements, and facade build-ups. We identify ambiguities, interface gaps, and discrepancies between consultant packages before touching a scale ruler. This rigorous reading ensures that our initial measurement captures the true spatial reality of the building rather than an idealized diagram, providing a sound foundation for every subsequent calculation.

02

Measure the Quantities

Once drawings are verified, we measure every building element in strict accordance with international measurement standards. We calculate net quantities across substructure, structural frame, upper floors, external envelope, internal partitions, floor finishes, and mechanical and electrical provisions. We never adopt broad approximations where detailed geometry exists. By breaking the proposed building down into discrete, measurable units of concrete, steel, timber, masonry, and glazing, we create an itemized framework. This granular quantification forms the baseline for both our elemental cost plan and subsequent contractor procurement, eliminating speculative allowances.

03

Price at Current Rates

Quantities are priced against live, verified supplier and subcontractor rates collected directly from the regional supply chain. We track current market movements across bulk materials, specialized trades, logistics, and site preliminaries. Rather than leaning on historic published cost indices that lag market realities, we price based on actual procurement conditions. Each unit rate reflects labor productivity, plant requirements, material delivery schedules, and current trade capacity. The resulting baseline figure reflects what reputable contractors must spend to deliver the specified quality within the anticipated construction timeline.

04

Write Down the Risks

An estimate without an explicit risk register is incomplete. Alongside the priced quantities, we compile an exhaustive register documenting every potential cost variable that cannot yet be priced with certainty. This includes unconfirmed ground conditions, existing structural interfaces in refurbishments, utility connections, statutory approvals, and market volatility. Each identified risk is assigned a calculated financial range rather than a generic contingency percentage. By making uncertainties visible, itemized, and transparent, we allow clients to manage specific exposure actively rather than relying on arbitrary safety margins.

05

Hand Over and Explain

A cost plan must be understood to be actionable. When our work is complete, we do not simply send an electronic spreadsheet. We deliver a bound elemental cost summary accompanied by an itemized cash-flow projection and the populated risk register. A partner presents the figures directly to the client and design team during an in-depth handover session. We explain the major cost drivers, walk through the measurement logic, review the risk allowances, and outline clear procurement recommendations so decisions can proceed with confidence.

Q

How early in design can a cost plan be prepared?

We can prepare an initial feasibility cost check or concept cost plan at the very earliest stages of design, including sketch proposals and massing options. Even before structural systems or internal partitions are resolved, our team establishes baseline volume, facade area, and structural bay models. We identify key cost drivers early, benchmark major building assemblies against international measurement standards, and test design alternatives before technical commitments are finalized. Appointing an independent cost consultant at concept design ensures that the architectural brief aligns with available capital from day one.

Request a proposal

pages.title: Fees & scope
pages.content:
Fees

All fees are stated in EUR excl. VAT and are fixed before work begins. We provide transparent pricing across seven defined services so clients know their exact commercial commitment.

01

Schedule of Fixed Fees

We provide seven core consultancy services priced on a transparent, fixed-fee schedule in EUR excl. VAT. Service 01, Feasibility cost check for one site and one massing option, is €2,400. Service 02, Second-opinion review of an existing estimate, is €1,900. Service 03, Concept cost plan based on schematic design, is €6,800. Service 04, Detailed cost plan for developed design packages, is €12,500. Service 05, Bill of quantities for contractor tender, starts from €18,000. Service 06, Tender review and contractor comparison, is €4,200. Service 07, Cost monitoring during active construction, is €1,150 per month.

02

What is Included in Our Deliverables

Each fee tier includes a complete, self-contained suite of professional deliverables. Our cost plans include an executive commercial summary, detailed elemental breakdowns structured by international measurement standards, cash-flow forecasts, and an itemized risk register. Feasibility checks provide comparative massing analyses and benchmark metrics. Tender reviews deliver a normalized comparison of subcontractor bids, flagging unpriced items and arithmetic errors. All commissions conclude with a structured handover presentation with the responsible partner. Invoices are issued on completion of each milestone with standard payment terms of 30 days.

03

What Parameters Influence the Fee

Our standard fees apply to typical commercial, educational, and residential developments within defined floor area bands. However, specific project complexities can require tailored scoping. Key factors that influence the final quotation include gross external floor area, the proportion of existing structural refurbishment versus new-build construction, site topography, and the number of distinct design options evaluated. When preparing your proposal within two working days, we review preliminary drawings to confirm whether standard fee levels apply or if complex phasing warrants a customized fixed price.

Q

What happens if the scope of work changes during design?

If the architectural brief expands significantly or major massing revisions occur after an estimating stage has commenced, we notify you immediately before undertaking additional work. Minor adjustments and iterative design developments are accommodated within our standard engagement. Where substantial redesign occurs, such as adding basement levels or introducing alternate structural typologies, we outline the required additional measurement hours and agree on a fixed fee variation in writing before proceeding. You will never receive unexpected charges or unapproved consulting fees.

Q

Are travel and site visits included in the fixed fee?

Standard site inspections and client handover meetings within the greater Rotterdam metropolitan area are included in our fixed service fees. For projects situated across the wider Netherlands or neighbouring European regions, required physical site visits and in-person municipal presentations are clearly specified in our initial proposal. We itemize any necessary travel expenses at cost without administrative markups. In all cases, the complete financial scope is agreed upon prior to engagement, ensuring total commercial transparency from start to finish.

pages.title: Cases
pages.content:
Cases

We price buildings across residential, civic, and educational sectors before the first contractor is engaged. Here is how three representative projects performed from initial cost plan to outturn.

01

Harbourside library

02

Timber housing terrace

03

Primary school extension

01

Public building

Harbourside Library Refurbishment

This project comprised the extensive civic refurbishment of an existing 3,200 m² municipal building. Sekisan Partners joined the consultant team at sketch design stage to establish early commercial viability. We prepared a concept estimate of €7.9 m, carefully quantifying structural interventions, acoustic upgrades, and facade remediation. During developed design, market pricing for heritage glazing moved upward, but our early risk allowances absorbed the variance. When the tender packages were returned by competing contractors, the lowest compliant tender came in at €8.1 m. The client proceeded to contract without cutting architectural scope or compromising civic interior finishes.

02

Residential

48-Home Timber Housing Terrace

This sustainable residential scheme involved a 48-home timber-clad terrace covering 5,600 m² of residential floor area. Appointed to establish cost control ahead of procurement, our team produced a detailed cost plan of €13.4 m based on developed architectural and structural packages. We measured timber frame quantities, modular wall panels, and civil groundworks with meticulous accuracy. The client utilized our itemized bill of quantities to run a competitive tender across specialized regional contractors. The awarded construction contract came in at €13.2 m, securing procurement certainty within 2% of our pre-tender estimate.

03

Education

Primary School Extension

We were appointed by an educational authority to deliver a second-opinion review of an existing estimate for a 1,450 m² primary school extension. Our initial review produced a revised baseline estimate of €4.6 m, introducing a transparent risk register for uncertain ground conditions and deep foundation piling. During excavation, poor soil bearing capacity required additional piling, drawing on the allocated risk line. Because the contingency was specifically earmarked, the final construction outturn came in at €4.75 m. Exactly half of the ground risk allowance was utilized, allowing the school to open on schedule within approved financial limits.

The lesson

Ground conditions were priced as a risk. When the piling came, half of that allowance was used and the school opened on schedule.

Q

How do our estimates compare against final tender returns?

Our cost plans are designed to predict true market outturn rather than provide optimistic targets. By measuring net quantities rigorously and pricing against live trade quotations, our figures align closely with competitive contractor tenders. Across our history since 2011, compliant contractor tenders have consistently aligned within narrow margins of our pre-tender estimates, as demonstrated across our library, housing, and school commissions. Where market prices shift between initial concept and procurement, our itemized risk registers and cash-flow projections provide clients with the data needed to make informed choices without reactive cost-cutting.

Request a proposal

pages.title: Cost letter
pages.content:
Letter

The Cost Letter is our quarterly intelligence bulletin analyzing material prices, subcontractor labor rates, and procurement conditions. Edited by Hana Sato, it provides objective cost data for developers, institutions, and architects.

01

Quarterly Market Intelligence

The Cost Letter is prepared by Hana Sato, who leads cost data research at Sekisan Partners. Each quarterly edition draws upon empirical pricing gathered directly from live contractor tenders, subcontractor returns, and regional material suppliers. Rather than echoing retrospective government indices or generalized macroeconomic commentary, the publication tracks specific movements across primary building trades, including ready-mix concrete, structural steel, timber systems, facade glazing, and mechanical installations. We highlight emerging supply chain constraints and trade capacity shifts to help clients forecast procurement budgets with greater accuracy.

02

First Issue: January 2027

The inaugural issue of the Cost Letter will be published in January 2027. Distributed free of charge in digital format, each issue includes clear graphical rate summaries, concise analytical commentary on quarterly price fluctuations, and practical guidance on mitigating procurement risk. By establishing an empirical record of actual market transactions, we aim to eliminate speculation from early building cost forecasting. Subscribers receive each quarterly report directly via email upon release, without marketing collateral or commercial sponsorship.

Sign up

Free, quarterly, first issue January 2027. No sponsors, no marketing.

Q

Who reads the Cost Letter?

The publication is written for property directors, public procurement officers, project managers, and lead architects who need dependable construction economics data. Readers use our quarterly rate analyses to benchmark feasibility budgets, check trade tenders against current market benchmarks, and anticipate inflationary pressures before committing capital. If your team is responsible for commissioning buildings or assembling capital investment programs, the Cost Letter delivers concise, verifiable market intelligence written directly by working quantity surveyors.

pages.title: Notes
pages.content:
Notes

Our professional notes share practical observations on cost planning, contractor procurement, and commercial risk management. We document lessons learned across our daily practice at Maaskade 41.

01

Practical Notes on Construction Economics

The Notes section serves as an archive of technical articles and commentary authored by our practice partners and senior estimating team. We write about real problems encountered during measurement, tender analysis, and site cost control. Topics range from the structuring of elemental risk registers to the forensic analysis of contractor preliminaries and the financial realities of low-carbon timber construction. Our objective is to demystify building economics and provide transparent, actionable knowledge to property owners and architectural collaborators.

02

Recent Articles and Editorial Themes

Our recent publications focus on three critical phases of building procurement. In 'Why the risk register comes first', we examine how early quantification of site and statutory uncertainties protects capital better than generic lump-sum contingencies. In 'Reading a tender comparison', Lukas Brandt explains how to normalize contractor bids to uncover disguised omissions and arithmetic errors. In our autumn cost briefing, Hana Sato provides an overview of quarterly price shifts across structural timber, masonry, and mechanical trades.

Q

How can readers submit topics for future articles?

We frequently address specific technical questions raised by clients, project managers, and design teams. If there is a particular aspect of building measurement, international measurement standards, or contractor procurement you would like us to analyze, you can send an inquiry directly to proposals@sekisan.example. Our team reviews incoming suggestions and regularly incorporates recurring industry challenges into our publication calendar, providing detailed case studies and methodical explanations grounded in daily professional practice.

Request a proposal

Privacy

Sekisan Partners respects your professional privacy and treats all client information with complete confidentiality. This policy outlines how we handle project data, correspondence, and technical drawings.

01

Data Handling and Project Information

Sekisan Partners, located at Maaskade 41, 3071 NB Rotterdam, Netherlands, acts as data controller for information submitted through our website and email correspondence. When you submit architectural drawings, site specifications, or procurement documents to proposals@sekisan.example, we use that material exclusively to evaluate the project scope, prepare fixed-fee proposals, and deliver agreed cost planning services. We do not sell, rent, or transfer your commercial drawings or personal contact information to third parties or marketing platforms under any circumstances.

02

Data Retention and Confidentiality Rights

Project drawings, tender schedules, and correspondence are retained securely within our encrypted studio archives for the duration of the engagement and any statutory record-keeping period required by commercial practice. Client documentation is accessible only to partners and staff directly assigned to the commission. You maintain the right to inspect, correct, or request the deletion of your personal contact data at any time by contacting our client desk at proposals@sekisan.example. All communications are governed by applicable data privacy regulations within the Netherlands.

pages.title: Terms of engagement
pages.content:
Terms

Our professional engagements are governed by clear, transparent terms established prior to commencing work. We provide fixed fees, defined delivery milestones, and equitable commercial terms.

01

Fixed Fees and Invoicing Terms

All consultancy fees quoted by Sekisan Partners are fixed prior to the commencement of work and stated in EUR excl. VAT. We do not charge variable hourly rates or unexpected administrative markups. Invoices are issued upon delivery of the agreed cost planning milestone, feasibility study, or tender report. Payment is due in full within 30 days from the invoice date. Where significant changes to the project brief or gross floor area occur during design, any scope variation is mutually agreed upon in writing before additional measurement work begins.

02

Scope of Service and Liability

Our deliverables are prepared with professional skill and diligence based on information provided by the client and design team, applying international measurement standards and verified market rates. Our cost plans represent independent expert opinions of probable construction cost and procurement risk at the date of preparation. Total aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with our services, whether in contract, tort, or otherwise, is strictly limited to the total fee paid for the specific service under engagement.

posts.title: Why the Risk Register Comes First
posts.excerpt: An early building estimate is only as reliable as the uncertainties it identifies, making an itemized risk register the true foundation of construction cost control.
posts.content:
In standard construction practice, the cost plan and the risk register are too often treated as separate documents prepared at different times. An architectural design is drawn, an estimator calculates quantities, unit rates are applied, and finally a flat percentage contingency is added at the bottom of the summary sheet. This conventional habit creates a dangerous illusion of precision. The itemized rows of concrete, structural steel, and facade glazing look exact because they carry decimal places, while the single contingency line conceals every genuine uncertainty surrounding ground conditions, structural interfaces, and statutory approvals.

At Sekisan Partners, we reverse that sequence. When our team begins evaluating a project from our Rotterdam studio, the risk register is opened before the first quantity is measured. Every construction project carries distinct categories of exposure that cannot be resolved through geometry alone. These include unconfirmed soil bearing capacities, utility diversions, hazardous material remediation in existing buildings, and unresolved detailing at structural junctions. If these uncertainties are left unquantified, they do not disappear; they simply emerge later as contractor claims and urgent budget revisions during construction.

Writing down risks from the outset transforms the financial conversation between the client, the architect, and the cost consultant. Instead of burying doubt within an arbitrary contingency figure—such as five or ten percent—we itemize each specific risk event, describe the potential commercial impact, and assign a calculated financial range based on empirical historical data. When evaluating an existing building refurbishment, for example, the risk register explicitly isolates the cost of uncovering concealed structural defects or rerouting undocumented services before design commitments become irreversible.

This level of transparency changes how design teams make decisions. When a client sees that poor ground conditions carry a quantified risk of several hundred thousand euros, geotechnical site investigations become an immediate priority rather than a deferred administrative task. As soil testing confirms site conditions, the corresponding risk allocation is either spent on engineered foundations or retired entirely from the budget. The capital is not locked away in a vague allowance; it is actively managed and released as physical certainty increases across each project milestone.

An itemized risk register also protects the integrity of architectural design during contractor procurement. When bids come in higher than expected, projects without an explicit risk breakdown inevitably resort to hasty value engineering, stripping away high-quality facade finishes, civic landscaping, or interior detailing. In contrast, when risks have been systematically documented and tracked against international measurement standards, the client and design team can differentiate between baseline trade costs and genuine unforeseen events, preserving core architectural intentions under market pressure.

Ultimately, our objective is to ensure that the figure approved at concept stage is the figure to which the building is delivered. A cost plan that ignores risk is merely a theoretical exercise in arithmetic. By identifying uncertainties early, giving each one an explicit price tag, and reviewing the register alongside the priced quantities at every design milestone, we provide building owners with genuine commercial certainty before the first contractor sets foot on site.
